new_statements.relation_note: Stress non-phonemic in all surveyed Lumi Subdistrict languages; default first non-schwa syllable; Aiku entry (incl. Yirkin village) has no stress remark of its own. Full text not downloaded (JSTOR / archive.org lending login); quote is verbatim scanned from the archive.org full-text-search API responses saved on by sibling checks, re-read by me.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Survey-wide (all Lumi Subdistrict languages Laycock lists, Aiku included): stress is not phonemic; by transcription convention it falls on the first syllable whose vowel is not schwa unless marked otherwise. No Aiku-specific phonological summary is given (entry runs (a)-(d) then the next language).
new_statements.secondary_stress: not mentioned in the snippets seen
new_statements.exceptions: Syllables containing schwa are skipped; stress is written only where it deviates from that default (in the 46-item Aiku list as re-keyed on TransNewGuinea one form is so marked: yimán 'breast'). '[a]' in the scanned snippet is Laycock's schwa symbol (not verified against the page scan; PDF is login-only).
new_statements.identity_note: Same work as A's index 1, re-reported because it does carry a stress statement. Laycock's 'Aiku' (Palei group; 790 speakers; villages Monandin, Sengi, Suau, Womerau, Yirkin; informant NR; recorded Nuku 7/67) is the pre-2007 Aiku [mzf] = Yangum Mon + Yangum Dey + Yangum Gel + Ambrak; Yirkin = Yirki, the single Yangum Gel village (ISO CR 2006-057). The stress sentence is a survey-wide convention for all Lumi Subdistrict languages listed, not an Aiku-specific finding, and the village that supplied the 1967 Aiku list is not stated; Glottolog attaches the paper to Yangum Mon (yang1296), Yangum (yang1303) and Yangum-Ambrak (yang1294), and the live yang1295 page links it only in its source list.
